description: A $4.8M ARR data center account suffers a catastrophic cooling failure that takes 40% of GPU fleet offline. Health plummets from 82 to 31. The CS team mobilizes a war room, orchestrates systematic recovery, and secures renewal plus $1.2M expansion -- proving 2,495% ROI on $185K CS investment.

phases.name: Pre-Crisis Baseline
phases.description: Account is healthy and performing well. Routine operations with stable KPIs. Subtle early-warning signals appear in thermal management trending slightly downward and preventive maintenance slipping, but overall health remains solidly in the healthy zone.

plot_points.description: Quarterly Business Review confirms strong GPU utilization at 78% and healthy expansion trajectory. VP Operations expresses satisfaction with platform stability.
Thermal Management Score dips from 97% to 93%, crossing below target threshold. CRAC unit in Zone B showing intermittent temperature spikes during peak GPU load.
Preventive Maintenance Compliance drops to 88% as ops team defers CRAC unit inspection to prioritize a new deployment. CSM notes this in weekly sync but no action taken.

csm_action.description: CSM flags deferred maintenance in weekly report, recommends scheduling CRAC inspection

phases.name: Crisis Event
phases.description: Catastrophic cooling system failure cascades through the data center. CRAC Unit B fails completely, causing thermal breach in 3 GPU rows. Emergency thermal shutdown takes 40% of GPU fleet offline. Training jobs abort mid-epoch, RMA requests flood in, and critical incident count spikes. Health score plummets from 78 to 31 in 10 days.

plot_points.description: CRAC Unit B compressor fails at 02:14 AM. Zone B ambient temperature rises from 22C to 38C in 47 minutes. Thermal protection triggers emergency GPU throttling on 3 rows (128 GPUs).
8 active training jobs abort mid-epoch. Training Job Completion Rate crashes to 35%. Data Center Manager triggers P1 incident protocol and pages VP Operations. CTO notified within the hour.

csm_action.description: CSM activates crisis protocol, schedules emergency bridge call with VP Operations and CTO within 2 hours

plot_points.description: Post-thermal-breach inspection reveals 14 GPUs with thermal damage requiring RMA. RMA Frequency Rate spikes to 4.4%. MTBF drops to 2,100 hours. Full $4.8M ARR now at risk as customer's CTO questions platform reliability.

VP Operations convenes emergency leadership meeting. GPU utilization at 38%, inference latency P95 ballooned to 320ms, distributed training efficiency collapsed. Customer threatens to evaluate competing platforms if recovery timeline exceeds 30 days.

phases.name: War Room
phases.description: CS team establishes a dedicated war room with daily standups. Support Engineering Lead deploys on-site for 3 weeks. Emergency hardware replacement approved and expedited. Temporary cooling supplemented with portable units. Health stabilizes in low 30s then begins climbing through 40s as emergency measures take hold.

plot_points.description: War room established with daily 30-minute standups. CSM, Support Engineering Lead, Data Center Manager, and VP Operations aligned on recovery roadmap. Three workstreams defined: (1) cooling restoration, (2) GPU replacement, (3) workload migration.

csm_action.description: CSM establishes war room cadence, creates shared recovery tracker, coordinates cross-functional workstreams

plot_points.description: Emergency hardware replacement approved: 14 replacement GPUs plus 2 portable cooling units shipped overnight ($95K). Support Engineering Lead on-site validates thermal containment strategy. Thermal Management Score recovers to 78%.

csm_action.description: CSM escalates to supply chain, secures 48-hour expedited shipping for replacement GPUs and portable cooling

plot_points.description: First batch of 8 replacement GPUs installed and validated. Workloads begin migrating back to restored capacity. GPU Utilization recovers to 52%. Two of eight aborted training jobs successfully restarted.

Week 4 war room review: health score at 48, trending upward. VP Operations acknowledges rapid response but demands a redundancy plan to prevent recurrence. CTO sets condition: renewal contingent on documented redundancy architecture.

phases.name: Systematic Recovery
phases.description: Methodical, week-by-week recovery across all five pillars. Remaining GPUs replaced, CRAC system upgraded with N+1 redundancy, preventive maintenance overhauled. GPU utilization climbs back through 60s to 75%+. Training job success rate normalizes. Health score crosses from at-risk (50s) through to healthy (70+) and stabilizes at 85. Expansion conversations resume as capacity utilization returns to pre-crisis levels.

plot_points.description: All 14 replacement GPUs installed and operational. Full cooling system restored with temporary redundancy. System Uptime back to 99.2%. RMA rate declining to 2.8%. Health score crosses 55 -- exiting critical zone into at-risk.

N+1 cooling redundancy plan approved by VP Operations ($65K investment). New CRAC unit ordered with automatic failover. Preventive maintenance program restructured to weekly thermal inspections. Health score reaches 65.

csm_action.description: CSM co-designs N+1 redundancy architecture with Support Engineering Lead, presents ROI analysis to VP Operations showing $4.8M ARR protection for $65K investment

plot_points.description: Health score crosses 70 -- back into healthy zone. GPU Utilization at 72%, Training Job Completion Rate at 93%, System Uptime at 99.7%. All aborted training jobs successfully completed. CTO sentiment shifts positive for first time since crisis.

Full recovery confirmed. Health score at 85, exceeding pre-crisis baseline of 82. N+1 cooling installed and validated. MTBF recovered to 9,200 hours. Thermal Management at 98%. Expansion Probability climbs to 62%. VP Operations requests expansion proposal for additional GPU capacity.

phases.name: Renewal & Expansion
phases.description: With health restored and redundancy proven, renewal discussions proceed with high confidence. The crisis response becomes a selling point: CS team's rapid mobilization demonstrates platform commitment. CTO approves 3-year renewal at $4.8M ARR plus $1.2M expansion for additional GPU racks with built-in redundancy. Final ROI: $185K CS investment protected $4.8M ARR and generated $1.2M expansion.

plot_points.description: Renewal kickoff meeting. CSM presents crisis recovery case study showing 54-point health score recovery (31 to 85) in 18 weeks. ROI deck quantifies $185K CS investment protecting $4.8M ARR. VP Operations champions renewal internally.

csm_action.description: CSM builds crisis-to-recovery narrative deck for renewal negotiation, quantifies ROI of CS intervention at 2,495%

plot_points.description: CTO approves 3-year renewal with enhanced SLA terms including guaranteed 4-hour MTTR and N+1 redundancy commitment. Expansion proposal for 2 additional GPU racks ($1.2M) submitted alongside renewal.
$4.8M renewal signed. $1.2M expansion order for 2 GPU racks with redundant cooling confirmed. Partner NPS score jumps to 72. Technical Champion Engagement at 88. Health score stable at 87.

decisions.title: Declare P1 Incident

options.option: Declare P1 and activate full incident response with executive notification
Treat as P2 incident and handle through standard support channels
Defer classification pending root cause analysis

decisions.outcome_description: Declaring P1 triggered immediate executive engagement, enabling war room formation within 24 hours. Fast escalation shortened recovery timeline by an estimated 3 weeks vs. standard P2 process.

decisions.title: Approve Emergency Hardware Replacement

options.option: Expedite 14 replacement GPUs via overnight shipping plus 2 portable cooling units ($95K)
Standard RMA replacement process (6-8 week lead time)
Partial replacement -- only replace 8 most critical GPUs ($55K)

decisions.outcome_description: Full expedited replacement restored GPU fleet in 3 weeks vs. 8 weeks for standard RMA. The $95K investment protected $4.8M ARR by keeping recovery within customer's 30-day deadline.

decisions.title: Implement N+1 Cooling Redundancy Plan

options.option: Full N+1 redundancy: additional CRAC unit with automatic failover ($65K)
Enhanced monitoring only: add thermal sensors and automated alerts ($12K)
No additional investment -- rely on improved maintenance schedule

evidence_refs: CTO set redundancy as condition for renewal
Root cause analysis showing single CRAC as single point of failure
ROI analysis: $65K investment protects $4.8M ARR (7,385% ROI)
decisions.outcome_description: N+1 redundancy eliminated the single point of failure that caused the crisis. This directly satisfied CTO's renewal condition and became a key proof point in the expansion proposal.

1-year renewal at $4.8M ARR with standard SLA, defer expansion
Decline renewal, pursue competitive RFP process

evidence_refs: Crisis recovery ROI of 2,495% on $185K CS investment

outcomes.title: $4.8M ARR Renewal Secured
